inlines.text: “When you square a negative number you get a positive number, so the graph of
Explain why this statement is incorrect.

answer.short: $y=x^2$ is the same as $y=(-x)^2$, but not $y=-x^2$. In $-x^2$, the negative sign is outside the square, so it does not get squared.
answer.worked:
$-x^2$ means $-(x^2)$: square $x$ first, then apply the negative sign. In contrast, $(-x)^2=x^2$ because the negative sign is inside the brackets.

Therefore $y=-x^2$ opens downwards, whereas $y=x^2$ opens upwards.

inlines.text: Which of the cards show the equation of a straight line and which show the equation of a parabola?

answer.short:
Straight line: A, C, F.

Parabola: B, D, E, G, H.
answer.worked:
A, C and F have the form $y=mx+c$, so their graphs are straight lines.

B, D, E and G have a non-zero $x^2$ term, so their graphs are parabolas. H is also quadratic:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(6-2x)^2\\y&=4x^2-24x+36.\end{aligned}$$
Straight line: A, C, F.

Parabola: B, D, E, G, H.

answer.worked: The lowest point is $(2,-1)$. The parabola opens upwards, so this is a minimum turning point.
The vertical symmetry line passes through the vertex, so its equation is $x=2$.
The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $y=3$, giving $(0,3)$.
The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $x=1$ and $x=3$, giving $(1,0)$ and $(3,0)$.
The minimum value is the $y$-coordinate of the vertex: $-1$.

answer.worked: The highest point is $(-1,4)$. The parabola opens downwards, so this is a maximum turning point.
The vertical symmetry line passes through the vertex, so its equation is $x=-1$.
The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $y=3$, giving $(0,3)$.
The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-3$ and $x=1$, giving $(-3,0)$ and $(1,0)$.
The maximum value is the $y$-coordinate of the vertex: $4$.

answer.worked:
Using the point $(-2,16)$:
$$\begin{align*}a^{-2}&=16\\\frac{1}{a^2}&=16\\a^2&=\frac{1}{16}\\a&=\frac14\end{align*}$$
The exponential base is positive, so $y=\left(\frac14\right)^x$, equivalently $y=4^{-x}$.

inlines.text: The height above the ground, in metres, of a person’s eyes varies directly with the square of the distance, in kilometres, that the person can see to the horizon.
A person whose eyes are 1.6 m above the ground can see 4.5 km out to sea.
How high above the ground, in metres, would a person’s eyes need to be to see an island that is 15 km out to sea? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be eye height in metres and $d$ be distance to the horizon in kilometres.
$$\begin{align*}h&=kd^2\\1.6&=k(4.5)^2\\k&=\frac{1.6}{4.5^2}\\h&=\frac{1.6}{4.5^2}(15)^2\\h&=\frac{160}{9}\text{ m}\\h&\approx17.8\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Moses finds that for a Froghead eel, its mass is directly proportional to the square of its length.
An eel of this species has a length of 72 cm and a mass of 8250 grams.
What is the expected length of a Froghead eel with a mass of 10.2 kg?
Give your answer to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $m$ be mass in grams and $l$ be length in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}m&=kl^2\\8250&=k(72)^2\\k&=\frac{8250}{72^2}\\10.2\text{ kg}&=10200\text{ g}\\10200&=\frac{8250}{72^2}l^2\\l&=\sqrt{\frac{10200\times72^2}{8250}}\\l&\approx80.1\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Use the positive square root because length is positive.

content.prompt:
A movie theatre has 200 seats. Each ticket currently costs $\$8$.

The theatre owners are currently selling all 200 tickets for each session. They decide to increase the price of tickets to see if they can increase the income earned from each movie session.

It is assumed that for each one dollar increase in ticket price, there will be 10 fewer tickets sold.

A graph showing the relationship between an increase in ticket price and the income is shown below.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, graph to the left of the response prompts
spec.description: Given black downward-opening income curve with positive-axis arrows, labelled major ticks and a rectangular grid. Dense dotted source subdivisions require final-size reconciliation.
spec.mathematics: For price increase x, income is I=(8+x)(200-10x)=-10x^2+120x+1600, on 0≤x≤20. The vertex is (6,1960); the displayed endpoints are (0,1600) and (20,0). Horizontal major ticks are 0,2,…,20; vertical major ticks are 0,200,…,2000.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve remains visible because students interpret it; teacher response calculations are separate.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What ticket price should be charged to maximise the income from a movie session?

answer.worked:
The graph has its maximum at a ticket-price increase of $\$6$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Ticket price}&=\$8+\$6\\&=\$14\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the number of tickets sold when the income is maximised?

answer.worked:
The maximum income read from the graph is $\$1960$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tickets sold}&=1960\div14\\&=140\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
The cost to the theatre owners of running each session is $\$500$ plus $\$2$ per ticket sold.

Calculate the profit earned by the theatre owners when the income earned from a session is maximised.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Cost}&=500+2\times140\\&=\$780\\\text{Profit}&=1960-780\\&=\$1180\end{aligned}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Gutter diagram above the area model
spec.description: Open gutter with a U-shaped near cross-section and lengthwise edges receding upwards and right. The near base is labelled w and the left upright is labelled h. The obscured left base edge is dashed. Source grey face shading is intentionally omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: The rectangular cross-section has width w and height h. No numerical dimensions or gutter length are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student-visible given.

spec.description: Unlabelled downward-opening parabola between the origin and w=40, with positive-direction axis arrows, A and w axis labels, and a single numbered tick at 40. No grid, vertical scale or vertex label. The source origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: A=-0.5w²+20w for 0≤w≤40. Axis extensions are presentation margins, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve remains student-visible because the task requires interpreting its maximum.

inlines.text: cm², of the cross-section can be modelled by the quadratic formula
A graph of this model is shown.
Find the width and height of the rectangle which will give the greatest possible area of the cross-section.

answer.worked:
The model is $A=-0.5w^2+20w$.

The maximum occurs halfway between the intercepts, by symmetry of the parabola.
$$\begin{align*}w&=\frac{0+40}{2}=20\text{ cm}\\A&=-0.5(20)^2+20(20)\\A&=200\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
Since the rectangle has area $A=wh$,
$$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{A}{w}\\h&=\frac{200}{20}=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Therefore, the width is $20\text{ cm}$ and the height is $10\text{ cm}$.

Examples of exponential models include population growth, compound interest, declining-balance depreciation and radioactive decay.

presentationRequirements: Growth remains left of decay. Each initial-value arrow targets a; each rate annotation identifies r within its corresponding factor. Review arrow endpoints at final size.

sourceAtom.label: Interpret exponential model from the equation

content.prompt: In each model, identify initial value, growth or decay, and increase/decrease per period.

answer.short: Initial value: 20; growth; increase of 10% per period.
answer.worked: The initial value is 20. The multiplier is 1.1, so the model represents growth of 10% per period.
$a=40$ and $r=0.2$. The factor $1+0.2=1.2>1$, so there is growth of $0.2\times100\%=20\%$ per period.
$a=40$ and $r=0.2$. The factor $1-0.2=0.8<1$, so there is decay of $0.2\times100\%=20\%$ per period.
$a=35$ and $r=0.5$. The factor $1+0.5=1.5>1$, so there is growth of $0.5\times100\%=50\%$ per period.
$a=1400$ and $r=0.32$. The factor $1-0.32=0.68<1$, so there is decay of $0.32\times100\%=32\%$ per period.
$a=7600$ and $r=0.44$. The factor $1-0.44=0.56<1$, so there is decay of $0.44\times100\%=44\%$ per period.
$a=3500$ and $1.12=1+0.12$. The factor is greater than 1, so there is growth of $0.12\times100\%=12\%$ per period.
$a=2300$ and $1.72=1+0.72$. The factor is greater than 1, so there is growth of $0.72\times100\%=72\%$ per period.
$a=180$ and $0.8=1-0.2$. The factor is less than 1, so there is decay of $0.2\times100\%=20\%$ per period.
$a=800$ and $0.6=1-0.4$. The factor is less than 1, so there is decay of $0.4\times100\%=40\%$ per period.
$a=1240$ and $0.65=1-0.35$. The factor is less than 1, so there is decay of $0.35\times100\%=35\%$ per period.
$a=5000$ and $1.175=1+0.175$. The factor is greater than 1, so there is growth of $0.175\times100\%=17.5\%$ per period.

answer.short: The graph decreases and the base $0.95$ is between $0$ and $1$.

content.prompt: The graph shows the number of bacteria $y$ at time $n$ minutes. Initially, when $n=0$, the number of bacteria is 1000.

spec.description: Given exponential curve on a rectangular grid, left of the response prompts. Positive axes have arrowheads. Horizontal grid spacing is 5 minutes and vertical grid spacing is 500 bacteria; labelled ticks retain the source values.
spec.mathematics: The curve passes through (0,1000), (20,2000), (40,4000) and (60,8000), reconstructed as y=1000*2^(n/20). Grid extends from n=0 to n=95 and y=0 to y=8000.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve remains visible because students must read and interpret it.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the number of bacteria at 40 minutes.

answer.worked: At $n=40$, the graph gives $y=4000$. There are 4000 bacteria.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
The number of bacteria can be modelled by $A\times b^n$ where $A$ and $b$ are constants.

Use guess and check to find, to two decimal places, an upper and lower estimate for the value of $b$. The upper and lower estimates must differ by 0.01.

answer.worked:
Initially, $A=1000$. At 40 minutes, the graph gives 4000 bacteria, so we need $1000b^{40}\approx4000$.

$$\begin{align*}
1000(1.03)^{40}&\approx3262<4000\\
1000(1.04)^{40}&\approx4801>4000
\end{align*}$$

Hence the lower estimate is 1.03 and the upper estimate is 1.04: $1.03<b<1.04$.

entries.description:
Linear relationships are in the form y = mx + c.
The graph is a straight line; so, the relationship is linear.
Quadratic relationships are in the form y = ax² + bx + c.
Their graph will not be a straight line; so the relationship is non-linear.
We can graph quadratic relationships the same way as linear relationships:
1. Construct a table of values using the equation.
2. Graph the table by using the columns as coordinates.
3. Join the points to form a smooth curve.

entries.description: Properties of the Parabola

A quadratic relationship y = ax² + bx + c produces a parabola-shaped graph.
Parabolas have these features:
• Line symmetry: Folding the parabola along this line makes both halves match.
• Vertex, or turning point: where the gradient changes direction.
The vertex is always on the axis of symmetry.
• The nature of the turning point (maximum or minimum) depends on coefficient of x²
• The maximum or minimum value is the y value at the turning point.

entries.description: Exponential Relationships

Exponential Relationships
Exponential relationships are in the form \(y=a^x\).
Their graph will not be a straight line; the relationship is non-linear.
We can graph exponential relationships the same way as before:
1. Construct a table of values using the equation.
2. Graph the table by using the columns as coordinates.
3. Join the points to form a smooth curve.
Consecutive \(y\) values change by a common ratio, which is the base number \(a\).

entries.description: Properties of the Exponential Curve

An exponential relationship y = a^x produces exponential curve graphs.
Exponential curves have these features:
• An asymptote: a line the graph approaches but never reaches.
• The nature of the graph (growth or decay) depends on the sign of x.
• Consecutive y values change by a common ratio, which is the base number a.
